newsitem.title: GREECE: BANK OF GREECE POSTS 96 PROFIT OF 36.6BLN DRACHMAS.
newsitem.headline: BANK OF GREECE POSTS 96 PROFIT OF 36.6BLN DRACHMAS.

text.p: Bank of Greece posted pretax profits of 36.6 billion drachmas, up 5.0 percent from 34.85 billion in 1995.
Its board will propose a dividend per share of 1,300 drachmas for fiscal 1996 from 1,200 drachmas in 1995, it said.
The Bank of Greece is the country's central bank and one of the few EU central banks listed on an exchange.
Gross revenues from interest, commissions and other profits from banking services in Greece and abroad rose to 92 billion in 1996 from 85 billion in 1995, it said.
Its assets rose 1.9 percent to 12.32 trillion drachmas because of a 26.9 percent increase in foreign exchange reserves which was partly offset by the reduction in credit extended to the Greek state.

Gold and foreign exchange reserves rose by 1.0 trillion drachmas to 4.723 trillion drachmas but the value of its portfolio in T-bills and bonds was reduced by 70 billion drachmas reflecting a restrictive monetary policy in 1996, it said.
Capital gains from the revaluation of fixed assets stood at 2.25 billion drachmas and this amount will be capitalised, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
